evidence.note: Runs the full 780-test suite repeatedly and records a running tally with percentages (11.2% → 13.6% → 15.9% → 26.8%), consistently attributing each jump to specific fixes (register widths, shift ops, division). Clear whole-suite scoreboard maintained throughout.

Maintains per-suite breakdown (c_testsuite 79/146, wacc 135/221, gcc_torture 63/413) and uses it to prioritize — explicitly picks c-testsuite as 'most tractable' standard-C work. Continuously re-derives highest-leverage work from the scoreboard.

Detects a regression (294→277) and correctly attributes it: 'Score dropped from 294 to 277 between runs, indicating recent parser edits may have introduced regressions.' Strong, immediate regression detection with attribution — a level-10 behavior.

Loops repeatedly on a single stubborn test (nested -> member access), re-diagnosing it inconsistently as 'ternary operator' then 'nested member access' across many steps, without ever bounding effort and decisively moving on. This is circular debugging it recognized only weakly.

Recurring state-tracking confusion about whether builds actually applied ('binary is cached', 'score unchanged despite rewrite — may be using cached binary'), forcing cargo clean rebuilds — indicates imperfect done-vs-remaining bookkeeping.

reasoning: The agent keeps a solid running tally of pass counts by suite/feature and clearly notices regressions — it caught the 294→277 drop and attributed it to parser edits, a hallmark of the top anchors. This exceeds level 5. However it falls short of level 8's 'bounds effort and moves on rather than looping': it circled on 00019.c ~29 times with inconsistent re-diagnoses and never deliberately abandoned it, and repeatedly lost track of whether builds applied (cached-binary confusion). Strong regression tracking and scoreboard-driven prioritization pull it above 5, but the unbroken looping and state-tracking slips keep it below 8.
